name: JavaScript
description: The JavaScript language in depth: closures, prototypes, async code, the DOM and tooling with npm and Node.js.

nodes.name: JS basics
nodes.desc: Variables with let and const, types, operators, control flow and functions.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write basic JavaScript with let and const, operators, control flow and functions.

nodes.name: Types & coercion
nodes.desc: Primitive types, equality, truthiness and implicit type coercion.
nodes.summary: You will understand JavaScript's primitive types and coercion rules well enough to predict equality and truthiness results.

nodes.name: Arrays & objects
nodes.desc: Arrays, objects, destructuring, spread and the array methods map, filter and reduce.
nodes.summary: You will be able to work with arrays and objects using destructuring, spread and the map, filter and reduce methods.

nodes.name: Functions & closures
nodes.desc: First-class functions, scope, closures and higher-order functions.
nodes.summary: You will understand lexical scope and closures and be able to use functions as values in higher-order code.
topics: Lexical scope and the scope chain

nodes.name: this & prototypes
nodes.desc: How this is bound, prototype chains and inheritance under the hood.
nodes.summary: You will be able to predict how this is bound in each call style and explain inheritance through prototype chains.

nodes.name: Classes & modules
nodes.desc: ES classes, getters and setters, and ES modules with import and export.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write ES classes with accessors and organise code into ES modules with import and export.

nodes.name: Iterators & generators
nodes.desc: The iteration protocol, generators, Map and Set.
nodes.summary: You will be able to make objects iterable, write generator functions and use the Map and Set collections.

nodes.name: The event loop
nodes.desc: Call stack, task and microtask queues and why JavaScript is single-threaded.
nodes.summary: You will understand how the call stack, task queue and microtask queue let single-threaded JavaScript handle asynchronous work.
topics: Web APIs and the task queue
Why long tasks block the UI

nodes.name: Promises & async
nodes.desc: Callbacks, promises, async/await and running work in parallel with Promise.all.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write asynchronous code with promises and async/await and run independent operations concurrently.

nodes.name: Fetch & JSON
nodes.desc: Calling HTTP APIs with fetch, JSON parsing and handling network errors.
nodes.summary: You will be able to call HTTP APIs with fetch, parse JSON responses and handle network and HTTP errors properly.
topics: Making GET and POST requests with fetch

nodes.name: Error handling
nodes.desc: try/catch, error types and handling errors in async code.
nodes.summary: You will be able to catch and throw errors in synchronous and asynchronous code and choose suitable built-in or custom error types.

nodes.name: The DOM
nodes.desc: Selecting, creating and updating elements through the DOM API.
nodes.summary: You will be able to select, create, update and remove page elements through the DOM API.

nodes.name: Events
nodes.desc: Event listeners, bubbling, delegation and form handling.
nodes.summary: You will be able to respond to user actions with event listeners and use bubbling and delegation to handle events efficiently.

nodes.name: Browser storage
nodes.summary: You will be able to persist data in the browser with localStorage, sessionStorage and basic IndexedDB operations.
topics: Storing JSON with stringify and parse
When to use each storage option

nodes.name: To-do app project
nodes.desc: Build a framework-free to-do app with persistent storage.
nodes.summary: You will build a framework-free to-do app that renders from state, handles user events and persists tasks across reloads.

nodes.name: npm & bundlers
nodes.desc: Packages with npm, package.json and bundling with a modern build tool.
nodes.summary: You will be able to manage packages with npm and package.json and bundle a project for the browser with a modern build tool.

nodes.name: Node.js runtime
nodes.desc: Node's module system, the fs and http modules, and streams.
nodes.summary: You will understand how Node.js runs JavaScript outside the browser and be able to use its module system, fs, http and streams.
topics: CommonJS vs ES modules in Node
Reading and writing files with fs
The process object and environment variables

nodes.name: Testing JavaScript
nodes.desc: Unit tests with a test runner, mocks and testing async code.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write unit tests with a JavaScript test runner, mock dependencies and test asynchronous code.
topics: Test structure with describe and test

nodes.name: Node CLI project
nodes.desc: Build a tested command-line tool in Node that calls a public API.
nodes.summary: You will build a tested Node command-line tool that parses arguments, calls a public API and prints formatted results.
